wa_okanogan.blurb: Okanogan takes in the far north of central Washington, from the North Cascades out to the Columbia River and up to the Canadian border. Sport climbing dominates, backed by a healthy amount of trad, some bouldering and a scattering of alpine objectives. Most routes fall between 5.8 and 5.12, with the heaviest concentration at 5.10 and 5.11. Mazama is the biggest hub, followed by Kettle Valley near Curlew and a string of crags around Tonasket and Oroville, including McLoughlin Canyon, Burge Mountain and Whistler Canyon. The Tonasket and Oroville cliffs are gneiss, mostly facing south and west with bolted lines; McLoughlin also holds longer trad. Kettle Valley is south-facing granite. The lower crags are best in late winter, spring and fall, since summer brings heat and rattlesnakes, while higher Burge Mountain stays more comfortable in summer.

ri_lincoln_woods.blurb: Lincoln Woods is a wooded state park a short drive from Providence, where hundreds of large glacial boulders sit among oak and maple trees around a pond. Nearly all of the climbing is bouldering, with only a few top-rope lines. Problems run from the very easiest up to V12, and the bulk of them sit between V0 and V5, so beginners and experienced boulderers both find plenty to work on. Heights range from small blocks to highballs of about 20 feet, and the styles include cracks, flakes, crimps, slopers, jugs, sit starts and traverses. Groupings such as Pond Cave Area, Sit Down Area, Super Crack 2 Area and Lost Crag Area spread the problems through the forest. Fall is considered the best season, and crash pads are advised.

az_flagstaff_area.blurb: The Flagstaff area spreads from Oak Creek Canyon through Walnut Canyon up to the San Francisco Peaks, and the rock changes with every stop. Sport climbing is the largest share, with a big helping of trad and a good number of boulder problems. Grades cluster between 5.10 and 5.12, with some 5.13. The Pit is a south-facing white limestone wall that stays dry and climbs through the winter. Mt. Elden Crags and the San Francisco Peaks offer volcanic rock such as dacite, with crimpy, slabby lines and long sport pitches, best from fall through spring. The Oak Creek Canyon Overlook is a basalt crag known for cracks and stemming. High elevation and a dry climate give a long season.

ca_highway_50_corridor.blurb: The Highway 50 corridor follows the American River Canyon up toward Echo Summit, and its granite crags mix trad, bouldering and sport. Trad is the largest share, bouldering comes next, and sport and top-rope routes round it out. Most routes fall between 5.7 and 5.11, with the heaviest concentration around 5.10, though a few reach into the 5.13s. Lover's Leap is a large, highly featured cliff with mostly multipitch routes of moderate to advanced difficulty and boulders at its base. Sugarloaf is a roughly 400-foot spire whose low elevation and south-facing aspect suit winter climbing. Phantom Spires is fully exposed, with a season from late fall to early summer and plenty of heat later. Echo Summit holds short bolted walls and low-angle slabs, good for beginners.

wy_ten_sleep_canyon.blurb: Ten Sleep Canyon lies just east of the town of Ten Sleep, with cliffs at roughly 7,000 to 7,500 feet that keep summer temperatures mild. It is overwhelmingly a sport climbing destination, with hundreds of routes spread across dozens of mini-crags, some beside the road and others a short hike in. The walls are dolomite and limestone, with bolted cracks, corners and jugs. Grades start around 5.7 but the weight sits in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, with a solid number of 5.13s and a few harder lines. Old Road Crags, Valhalla, Mondo Beyondo and French Cattle Ranch are among the biggest sectors. A few boulder problems and a little ice are also found in the canyon.

ct_western_coastal_slope.blurb: Western Coastal Slope covers the western side of Connecticut, a densely settled stretch with many small crags and boulder fields tucked into state parks and forests. Bouldering makes up most of the climbing, with trad second and a little sport and top-rope. Boulder problems mostly run from the easiest grades to about V5, with a thinner tail up to V10, while roped routes span 5.4 to 5.12. West Rock State Park sits on a ridge of dolerite; its west-facing cliffs warm quickly in the sun, which makes them a good cold-weather choice, and the sport development there is mostly on slabby ground at the south end. Sleeping Giant State Park offers short trad cliffs with loose rock in places. Bald Rock Basin holds the largest cluster of boulders.
